title: Appraisal Order Grace in Rate Lock Commitment Extension Disputes
content:
**Order grace by type of appraisal order (Rate Lock Commitment extension charge disputes).**

When the appraisal ordering days of a disputed **Rate Lock Commitment** extension are worked out, an order grace is subtracted. The appraisal ordering days are the calendar days counted to the date the appraisal order was placed, less the order grace, never below zero. The grace depends on the file's **Appraisal Order**:

| Appraisal order | Order grace (days) |
|---|---|
| Placed with rush turn time (any report type) | 1 |
| No rush; Larkspur Complex Property Appraisal (Form 1004 Jumbo) | 5 |
| No rush; Larkspur Small Residential Income Appraisal (Form 1025) | 5 |
| No rush; any other report type | 3 |

**Rule as stated.** The order grace depends on the order. An order placed with rush turn time has the rush order grace of 1 day. An order without rush for a Larkspur Complex Property Appraisal (Form 1004 Jumbo) or a Larkspur Small Residential Income Appraisal (Form 1025) has the complex order grace of 5 days. Any other order has the standard order grace of 3 days.

### Hypothetical cases

- A rush Larkspur Complex Property Appraisal (Form 1004 Jumbo) ordered 9 days into the count: rush governs, so the grace is 1 day and the ordering days are 8.
- A non-rush Larkspur Small Residential Income Appraisal (Form 1025) ordered 4 days into the count: the grace is 5 days, and the ordering days are 0 (never below zero).
- A non-rush Larkspur Single-Family Appraisal (Form 1004) ordered 4 days into the count: the grace is 3 days, and the ordering days are 1.
